findings.governingReading: Shirou’s consciousness disconnects like a severed wire.
findings.explanation: The English replaces loss of connection with general fragmentation, weakening the route’s recurring circuitry model.

findings.highlight: I am the bone of my sword.
findings.governingReading: The narration states directly that Shirou’s body is made of swords.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes a familiar incantation line, changing body composition into the metaphorical “bone” formula.

findings.governingReading: His body is already beyond saving.
findings.explanation: “Dying” removes the explicit point of no return.

findings.highlight: I want to keep my memory for as long as I can.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が自分のままでいる事に、指を食うほど執着している。
findings.governingReading: Shirou clings with self-devouring intensity to remaining himself.
findings.explanation: The English narrows existential self-continuity to retaining memory and removes the consuming force of attachment.

findings.highlight: I probably won’t remember what I need to do.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分が誰か、何をするかを、きっと無くしてしまっている
findings.governingReading: Even if he arrives, Shirou will surely have lost both who he is and what he is to do.
findings.explanation: The English drops identity entirely and weakens certainty to probability and loss to failed recollection.

findings.highlight: So I have to fulfill my role.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえは、おまえの役目を、果たさないと。
findings.governingReading: A surviving voice addresses Shirou as “you” twice and commands him to fulfill his role.
findings.explanation: The English changes the dissociated second-person self-command into ordinary first-person resolve.

findings.highlight: I couldn’t breathe if I had all day to do it.
findings.evidenceJa: たった一息の空気が、一日かけても吸えずにいる
findings.governingReading: Even given an entire day, Shirou remains unable to draw a single breath of air.
findings.explanation: The English turns an experienced time-dilated failure into a hypothetical inability.

findings.highlight: All the shards of my existence are gathered onto a tiny foothold.
findings.evidenceJa: 爪の先ほどの足場に、全存在を留まらせる
findings.governingReading: Shirou holds his entire existence on a foothold no larger than a fingernail tip.
findings.explanation: The English invents shards of existence and removes the exact fingernail scale and act of holding fast.

findings.governingReading: The reason for action is lost in the sequence from principle to purpose.
findings.explanation: “Meaning of behavior” is unnatural and collapses reason into the adjacent existential meaning.

findings.highlight: The meaning behind my existence disappears.
findings.evidenceJa: 何の為に誰の為に存在しているのか消失した
findings.governingReading: Shirou loses for what and for whom he exists.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes existential meaning and removes both purpose and beneficiary.

findings.evidenceJa: その腕が動く事はない。
findings.governingReading: That arm will move under no possible reason.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the arm and turns a distanced reference into ordinary possession.

findings.evidenceJa: 人工の知能がなくとも
findings.governingReading: Even without artificial intelligence, machines in this world weave dreams.
findings.explanation: The English directly replaces artificial intelligence with human intelligence, reversing the machine-specific premise.

findings.highlight: A small hope that I remembered until the very end.
findings.evidenceJa: 果たされるべき、小さな希望
findings.governingReading: The small hope remembered to the end is something that must be fulfilled.
findings.explanation: The English preserves final memory but removes the obligation that drives the dead mechanism onward.
